title: Certified Randomness without Structure Against Shallow-Query Adversaries
abstract: In a recent breakthrough, Yamakawa and Zhandry (J. ACM 2024) constructed a proof of quantumness in the quantum random oracle model (QROM) in which the quantum prover samples a codeword preimage of a publicly computable function H. They conjectured that given any H, a successful prover must sample their preimage from a high-entropy distribution over possible answers. If true, this would give a certifiable randomness protocol in the quantum random oracle model. As partial evidence for their conjecture, Yamakawa and Zhandry proved the security of their certifiable randomness protocol assuming the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. We prove the security of the certifiable randomness protocol of Yamakawa-Zhandry unconditionally, without relying on the unproven Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, against low query-depth quantum adversaries: specifically, adversaries that make up to o(\log λ) adaptive quantum queries to the random oracle.

bite.hook: We prove the security of Yamakawa and Zhandry's certifiable randomness protocol unconditionally.
tldr: Proved the security of a quantum certifiable randomness protocol against low query-depth adversaries.
Applied a proof framework that operates unconditionally without relying on unproven conjectures.
Demonstrated security against quantum adversaries making up to o(log lambda) adaptive queries.
bite.whyItMatters: Generating certified random numbers is crucial for cryptography and secure computing, and proving security without unverified assumptions makes it bulletproof.
bite.eli5: If you want to flip a coin and prove to someone else that it is truly random and not rigged, quantum mechanics helps. Scientists just proved a secure way to do this without needing extra unproven mathematical assumptions.

glossary.shortDef: An idealized cryptographic model where a hash function is treated as a random black box accessible to quantum computers.
glossary.eli5Def: A theoretical testing ground where a cryptographic function acts like a completely unpredictable quantum black box.

glossary.shortDef: An input that evaluates to a given output under a specific function.
glossary.eli5Def: The original password or input you put into a machine to get a specific output.

glossary.shortDef: Queries made to an oracle where each question depends on the answers received from previous questions.
glossary.eli5Def: Asking a magic box questions where your next question depends entirely on what the box answered just before.
